'''Markku Leskelä''' (born 1950) is a [[Finland|Finnish]] chemist and professor emeritus at [[University of Helsinki]], known for his leading research in [[atomic layer deposition]] (ALD).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.helsinki.fi/kemia/epaorgaaninen/personnel/leskela.htm|title=Markku Leskelä - Professor of Inorganic Chemistry|website=www.helsinki.fi}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tuhat.halvi.helsinki.fi/portal/fi/persons/markku-leskela(78010015-5f49-49b7-b712-54b1b327ac7b).html|title=Markku Leskelä - Helsingin yliopiston tutkimusportaali - Helsingin yliopisto|website=tuhat.halvi.helsinki.fi}}</ref>

Markku Leskelä was the leader of the [http://www.aldcoe.fi/ Finnish Centre of Excellence in ALD] (2012-2017) by the [[University of Helsinki]] and [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland]].

Markku Leskelä started ALD research (then called [[atomic layer epitaxy]]) in the early 1980s at [[Helsinki University of Technology]] (nowadays [[Aalto University]]) with Prof. Lauri Niinistö.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aldcoe.fi/events/finald40.pdf|title=Exhibition material "40 Years of ALD in Finland - Photos, Stories"|date=November 29, 2014|access-date=September 20, 2016}}</ref> In 2012, he received the ALD Innovation Prize at the international ALD conference.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://aldhistory.blogspot.fi/2016/08/ald-innovation-prize-to-dr-suvi-haukka.html|title=ALD Innovation Prize to Dr. Suvi Haukka, ASM|last=Puurunen|first=Riikka|date=August 3, 2016|access-date=September 20, 2016|website=aldhistory.blogspot.fi}}</ref>
